chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf) and finished it when the sun set. He (peace be upon him) said: The two cycles (Rak'atayn) became obligatory upon him at that time, so let him pray them before the Maghrib prayer.
ai.seo_question: When should the two cycles of Tawaf prayer be performed if the sun sets during the circumambulation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific timing for the two rak'ahs of Tawaf when sunset occurs during the circumambulation, ruling that they must be performed before the Maghrib prayer to avoid merging with it. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the distinct identity of the Tawaf prayer while adhering to the established prayer times, ensuring the ritual's completeness without delay. It serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims navigating the transition between ritual acts and obligatory daily prayers during the critical moment of sunset.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws from a man who circumambulated the Obigatory Tawaaf, and was free from his Tawaaf when the sun set. Heasws said: ‘The (Praying of the) two Cycles were Obligated upon him during that time, so let him Pray these two before the Magrib (Salaat)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who performs obligatory Tawaf and completes it at sunset. He (the Imam) said, ‘At that hour two Rak‘at Salat (prayer) become obligatory on him and he must perform them before sunset.’”
